To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activity of a single cortical neuron can be used to control a BMI actuator, and that this neuron, called a “master” cell, is preferentially targeted by the learning process.
operant conditioning of neuronal activity in rat motor cortex induces a preferential increase of firing rate and a decrease of firing rate variability for the conditioned neuron.

operant conditioning of neuronal activity in rat motor cortex during a brain-machine interface task induces the preferential modification of a single “master” neuron that acts as a trigger for the reconfiguration of the local network activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of brain-machine interfaces (BMIs), in which the subject learns the volitional control of a prosthetic device by operant conditioning.
the development of novel methods for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.
the study of the neural mechanisms underlying operant control of a brain-machine interface.

the cortical circuit reorganization induced by operant conditioning preferentially affects the neuron whose activity controlled the actuator during the learning phase.

the operant conditioning induces the formation of a master neuron, which leads in time the reorganization of neuronal activity in the local network.

the “master” neuron is induced by operant conditioning during a brain-machine interface task.
